newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Most Asia stocks zoom ahead as Dow sets new record.
newsitem.headline: Most Asia stocks zoom ahead as Dow sets new record.

text.p: Most Asia stock markets, led by Japan, raced ahead on Tuesday after Wall Street set another record overnight.
Shares in Tokyo pushed through the key 20,000-point barrier and Sydney's All Ordinaries reached a record but Thailand and South Korea failed to catch the enthusiasm and stocks headed lower.
The Dow gained 143 points, or 2.03 percent, to 7,214 on Monday on expectations of a cut in the capital gains tax and a belief that any further interest rate increases would be modest.
"Stocks rallied almost across the board," Kunihiro Hatae, general manager at Tokyo Securities Co Ltd, said of the rally in Tokyo on Tuesday.
At 0630 GMT, the key Nikkei-225 Index was up 666.17 points, or 3.41 percent, at 20,180.92. The market was closed on Monday.

"Worries over downside risks have diminished recently..., and the U.S. stocks' surge lifted the Nikkei...more steeply than expected," said Hisao Suzuki, deputy general manager at Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd.
Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index was up 181.19 points, or 1.35 percent, to 13,580.53 after reaching a high of 13,679.92.
However, traders were divided over how much further the market could advance or whether it will fall victim to profit-taking.
"It is likely that the market will stay at current levels and I think at this level people should take profit," said Sunny Chan, senior research manager at Seapower Securities.
Wall Street's advance also helped boost Philippine stocks after more than a week of sharp declines. Fresh domestic economic data buoyed sentiment.
Philippine stocks gained 40.11 points, or 1.47 percent, to close at 2,776.53.

Traders said the overall bearish sentiment that had gripped the Philippine market for more than a week had ebbed. Monday's better-than-expected inflation figures and solid trade data on Tuesday helped underpin the advance.
Singapore stocks followed the Dow and posted early gains, and a rebound in property stocks helped the market move higher.
The Straits Times Index was up 29.49 points, or 1.45 percent, at 2,058.09.
Indonesian shares firmed 3.843 points, or 0.59 percent, to 656.630, while Taiwan shares defied a bout of profit-taking and ended up 24.84 points, or 0.30 percent, at 8,294.27.

Australian stocks hit a record high of 2,518.5 just before noon, led by gains in New York and Tokyo, before easing slightly. By late afternoon the All Ordinaries Index was up 20.1 points, or 0.81 percent at 2,512.8.
In New Zealand, a lower interest rate environment helped push shares up 28.63 points, or 1.26 percent, to 2,305.24.
But some markets bucked the trend.
Malaysian shares turned lower after a firmer opening. Stocks were off 5.31 points, or 0.48 percent, at 1,089.66.
"There is some selling of shares by those who have been holding on for a while. That is pulling down the index," one dealer said.
Thai shares turned lower after opening higher on speculation that March export figures could show some improvement. The SET Index was off 4.91 points, or 0.74 percent, at 655.19.
Korean shares were lower overall on profit-taking in large-cap shares, although paper makers and pharmaceutical firms advanced. The composite index was off 3.30 points, or 0.47 percent, at 701.57.
